To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Mach cone structure is strongly influenced by the viscosity of the medium, that it is possible to reproduce the analytical result for the two-particle correlation in the case of a viscous medium, that the viscosity of the matter is crucial for the formation of the Mach cone and that a viscous medium leads to a stronger deformation of the Mach cone than an ideal fluid.
(i) the viscosity of the matter affects the structure of the Mach cone, and (ii) the structure of the two-particle correlation is affected by the viscosity of the medium.
the viscosity of the medium is responsible for a smooth transition from an ideal to a viscous Mach cone and that the structure of a Mach cone is determined by the viscosity of the matter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the microscopic properties of the matter on the structure and evolution of Mach cones.
the formation of conical structures in a microscipically transport model and the comparison with the analytical approximation.
the study of the transition of ideal to viscous conical structures in a microscoping transport model.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can describe the transition from the ideal fluid limit to the viscous fluid limit in BAMPS.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of the Mach cones in a microscopic transport model can be used as an observable to extract transport properties of the medium.
the structure of Mach cone is very robust against the variation of the viscosity of the matter and the interaction between projectile matter.
the Mach cone structure in a viscous medium can be reproduced with a non-viscous model by using an effective cross section.
